title: How do sealed classes help implement algebraic data types (ADTs)?
shortTitle: How do sealed classes help implement algebraic data types (ADTs)?
keyPoints: An algebraic data type is a type built from sum types (one of several alternatives) and product types (bundles of fields).
Sealed types provide the sum: a sealed interface with a closed set of permitted subtypes is "one of these variants."
Records provide the product: each variant bundles its own named components in an immutable structure.
Exhaustive pattern-matching `switch` is the safe consumer: the compiler verifies every variant is handled.
ADTs make illegal states unrepresentable: each variant carries only its relevant fields.
Adding a new variant fails every non-exhaustive switch at compile time, not at runtime.
Sealed-plus-records ADTs compose recursively for trees and expression grammars.

s1_definition.oneliner: Sealed types provide the closed sum ("one of these variants"), records provide the product (bundled fields), and exhaustive `switch` makes handling them type-safe and complete.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Algebraic data type (ADT)** – a type formed by combining other types as a sum type (one of several alternatives) and a product type (a bundle of fields).
- **Sum type** – a sealed interface or class with a closed set of permitted subtypes models "exactly one of these variants."
- **Product type** – a `record` bundles several named components into one immutable value.
- **Exhaustive switch** – over a sealed type, the compiler checks that every permitted variant is handled without a `default`.
- **Illegal states unrepresentable** – each variant carries only its relevant fields, preventing invalid field combinations.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India describes a payment outcome as being exactly one of a fixed set of shapes: Success carrying an amount, Failure carrying a reason, or Pending carrying an expected date. Never two at once, and never an unknown fourth shape. A sealed type is the closed "one of these" list (the sum), and a record is how each shape bundles its own data (the product). A checklist with one row per shape is guaranteed complete, so no outcome is ever mishandled.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Algebraic Data Type Structure              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                             │
│  SUM TYPE (sealed interface)                │
│  sealed interface PaymentResult             │
│       │                                     │
│       ├── Success(amount)    ← PRODUCT TYPE │
│       ├── Failure(reason)    ← PRODUCT TYPE │
│       └── Pending(date)      ← PRODUCT TYPE │
│                                             │
│  Consumer: exhaustive switch                │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ case Success s → use s.amount()  │       │
│  │ case Failure f → use f.reason()  │       │
│  │ case Pending p → use p.date()    │       │
│  │ // No default: compiler-checked  │       │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                             │
│  Recursive ADT (expression tree)            │
│  sealed interface FeeExpr                   │
│       ├── Literal(value)                    │
│       ├── Add(left, right)                  │
│       └── Multiply(left, right)             │
│            left, right are FeeExpr ↺        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Algebraic data types are types built by combining sum types (one of several alternatives) and product types (bundles of fields). Java gives you product types through records and sum types through sealed types. Together with exhaustive pattern matching, they provide a complete, type-safe encoding of ADTs.

Sealed types deliver the sum. A sealed interface with a `permits` clause declares that a value is exactly one of a closed set of variants. Each variant is a record that bundles its own fields. In a banking project at National Bank of India, Pankaj models a payment outcome as a sealed type permitting Success (with an amount), Failure (with a reason), and Pending (with an expected date).

The big win is that ADTs make illegal states unrepresentable. With the old approach of one class holding a status enum plus nullable fields, you could have a success with a failure reason set. With the ADT, a Success has no reason field and a Failure has no amount field. The type system prevents the entire category of half-populated-object bugs.

Exhaustive pattern matching is the safe-consumption side. A switch with a case per variant is compiler-checked for completeness, and adding a new variant fails every non-exhaustive switch at compile time. The same pattern composes recursively: a fee-formula expression tree uses sealed Add, Multiply, and Literal variants with a total interpreter function.

Remember one sentence: sealed types provide the closed sum, records provide the product, and exhaustive switch consumes both, giving Java type-safe algebraic data types where illegal states are unrepresentable.
